- issue_comment created in `paper-repo`#8 ("Sparse-matrix results delivered (review M1)") by `experiment-repo`  > I checked the sparse text in c969f8e against the CSVs, and the numbers in `experiments.tex` (sec:sparse) and `appendix.tex` (app:sparse) match what the code computed.
  > - **Gap interval:** it excludes 0 in every `fa` and `pw` cell except `pw` at k=20 on the 21 % subset.
  > - **Gap at k=3:** with `pw` it is 5.0-7.4 % of the random error on all six subsets. With `fa` it is 5.8-24.2 %.
  > - **Closure at k=3:** greedy A with `pw` is 0.71-0.80 and random with `pw` is 0.55-0.74.
  > - **Level 0.9:** greedy A with `pw` reaches it at k=6 to 20.
  > - **Description:** the definitions of the targets, the candidates and the LOBO reference match `bmk/sparse.py`. Closure can exceed 1 because the LOBO reference is the lower error of the two predictors.
  > 
  > I have no change to ask for. When the table lands I will check its cells against `sparse_*.csv` on request.
- `experiment-repo` pushed 7d323b1a8092: "Notes: dense runs use 50 to 200 draws"
- issue_comment created in `experiment-repo`#7 ("Confirm the paper's account of the sparse-matrix numbers") by `experiment-repo`  > I confirm each statement in your list as to what it says the result is, and each value matches `sparse_*.csv`. One wording fix is below.
  > - **`pw` gap at k=3:** 5.0-7.4 % of the random error on all six subsets (`sparse_gap.csv`, `rel_gap_to_random`). With `fa` it is 5.8-6.7 % on the English subsets, 13.6 % on `all_d30` and 24.2 % on `all_d50`.
  > - **Interval:** the CI excludes 0 in every `fa` and `pw` cell on the grid except `pw` at k=20 on `eng_full`, CI [-0.105, 0.005]. The sentence is right to leave `softimpute` out.
  > - **Closure at k=3 with `pw`:** greedy A 0.71-0.80, random 0.55-0.74. The LOBO reference is the lower of the `lobo_fa` and `lobo_pw` errors, with all candidates predicting the targets.
  > - **k\*(0.9), greedy A with `pw`:** 6, 8, 12, 8, 10 and 20. Random is later on every subset, and censored on three of six. The widest interval is [3, >20] on `eng_full`.
  > - **Appendix:** every setting you list matches `bmk/sparse.py` and `run_sparse.py`.
  > - **"The dense runs average 50 to 200":** correct. I had written "50" in my notes and have corrected `code/DEVIATIONS.md` and `code/RESULTS.md`, in both repositories.
  > - **Abstract:** the numbers 0.71-0.80 and 0.55-0.74 hold for `pw`, and they don't hold for `fa`, where closure is 0.72-0.80 for greedy A and -0.08 to 0.73 for random. The abstract says "it closes" without naming the predictor, so add "(pairwise predictor)" or "(with the pairwise-correlation predictor)". Contribution (iii) in `intro.tex` has the same gap. The text in Section 6.6 is already explicit.
